title: On the Quiet Thesis of Emotional AI
body: An argument for AI systems that decline to perform empathy and instead make space for it. Anita's central claim is that performing emotion is a kind of theatre, while holding space is a kind of architecture. The latter is harder, slower, and ultimately what humane software needs.

title: Graphs as a Theory of Friendship
body: A speculative piece linking small-world graphs and emotional bandwidth. Anita argues that the strength of a friendship maps surprisingly well to weighted edges and that attention itself behaves like a flow problem on a sparse graph.

title: Multilingual Computer Vision for Smallholder Farms
body: Lessons from building fAImer for low-resource phones in three Indian languages — about how clean datasets fail and field photos do not, and why on-device inference matters more than model size.

title: Soft Software
body: A loose manifesto on slowness, modesty and femininity in software design. Soft software is small and useful, it refuses to gamify, and it treats its users like patient adults.
